August 9, 2025

*TINGOG, Speaker Romualdez deliver rice and blankets to flood-affected families in Marikina*

TINGOG Party-list, in coordination with House Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez, distributed rice and blankets to families in Marikina City on Thursday following recent flooding brought about by prolonged monsoon rains.

Representatives Yedda Romualdez, Jude Acidre, and Andrew Romualdez led the relief operations in two barangays. In Barangay Tumana—where areas surrounding Singkamas Court are among the lowest in elevation and were affected by the flood—1,000 families received bags of rice and more than 500 blankets. The distribution was conducted alongside Marikina District 2 Representative Miro Quimbo, former Representative Stella Quimbo, Councilor Ziffred Ancheta, and Barangay Captain Akiko Centeno.

A second wave of assistance was held at Malanday Elementary School in Barangay Malanday, where 1,000 additional rice bags and over 1,000 blankets were provided, with the support of Marikina District 1 Representative Marcy Teodoro and Mayor Maan Teodoro.

“It’s hard to imagine the worry of a mother who doesn’t know where the next meal will come from after a flood,” said Rep. Yedda Romualdez. “That’s why we came—not just to bring rice, but to bring comfort, to be present, and to let every family here know that they are seen, they are remembered, and they are not alone.”

Rep. Jude Acidre noted the importance of local coordination in ensuring timely delivery of aid.

“When families are in crisis, presence matters,” said Acidre. “We thank our partners in Marikina for working with us to ensure this assistance reached affected residents without delay.”

The rice distribution is part of TINGOG’s broader relief efforts in areas affected by recent monsoon rains across Metro Manila and nearby provinces. Similar operations have been conducted in Pasay, Manila, Caloocan, and other cities in NCR.

TINGOG continues to work closely with local government units to deliver timely and targeted support to affected families. 

Photos courtesy of TINGOG Party-list.
